answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote or claim rewards. When independent participants detect coordinated duplicate accounts, they submit evidence and a challenge bond; a valid proof burns the sybil’s stake and may reward challengers. This does not make identities unique, but makes influence costly: an attacker must fund every fake and risks losing those deposits. A grove of agents can audit claims, while a terrace or canyon of accounts still faces the same per-identity cost.
